trust.title: Kill switches are {em}.
trust.lead: Autonomy only works with a hard floor under it. You can stop any Darwin instantly, it writes down every action before taking it, and it is born with rules it cannot rewrite or be talked out of.

kill.guarantee: Guaranteed ≤ 5 s · no consent needed from the Darwin
kill.note: A killed Darwin is never resurrected. This spawns a new one.

audit.label: Write-before-act audit log
audit.title: No log, no action.
audit.caption: Hashes computed live in your browser with SHA-256. Change one record and every record after it stops verifying.

constitution.label: Constitution · signed into the genome
constitution.title: It can't be talked out of its rules.

forbidden.unlisted: Any category not on the list

constitution.caption: 15 allowed categories (whitelist) · 7 forbidden classes, whatever the profit.

ladder.label: Graded response
ladder.title: Machines can slow it. Only humans end it.
ladder.caption: You, the owner, can pause, lock spending, block reproduction, disable any neuron or kill — at any time.

killSwitch.value: polled at every heartbeat, every graph-node boundary and right before every side effect; raises a KillSignal that evolved code can't catch

failsClosed.value: if the switch can't be read, the Darwin treats itself as killed; once tripped it stays tripped; egress is cut in parallel

auditRecord.value: {'{'}seq, prev_hash, ts, kind, payload, hash{'}'}; hash = sha256 of the canonical record; first prev_hash is 64 zeros

noLogNoAction.value: every intent is written before acting and closed by an outcome; if the write fails, the Darwin halts

anchoring.value: a daily per-Darwin Merkle root, then a fleet-wide root published on-chain; a diverging anchor is treated as tampering

constitution.value: screened deterministically over structured fields — never by an LLM; the genome refuses to boot on an incoherent rule set

genomeSigning.value: Ed25519; the platform's private key lives in an HSM/KMS and never enters a sandbox

escalationDeadlines.value: captcha 15 min · KYC 72 h · approval 24 h · info 7 days; a missed deadline is a deterministic deny

evolution.title: It rewrites itself.{br}{em}
evolution.lead: When the same mistake keeps happening, a Darwin may propose a change to its own code. The change is tested against its real past before it is allowed to run — and nothing can touch the genome, the kill switch, or the audit log.

propose.title: Propose
propose.body: The coding tier writes a diff to its own soma and states the behaviour it expects to change.

validate.title: Validate
validate.body: The genome's validator checks the diff — then the platform checks it again, outside the sandbox.

replay.title: Replay
replay.body: Old and new code replay the same real history in a fresh microVM, scored by the same fitness.

promote.title: Promote
promote.body: Only a better score is merged and hot-swapped into the running body. Same life, same wallet.

b.name: Patch B
b.verdict: Rejected · archived as a negative lesson

fitness.label: Fitness · weights frozen in the genome
fitness.note: One violation outweighs ten times its stake in profit. A Darwin can't buy its way out of breaking the rules.

legend.gen0: Gen 0 · the mother — 13 neurons, keeps living
legend.gen1: Gen 1 · buds at ≥ $25 profit with half the surplus
legend.gen2: Gen 2 · children that thrive bud again

lineage.title: Children inherit {em}, not code.
lineage.lead: Success spreads. At reproduction the mother distils what worked into a sealed, signed layer on top of its genome. Each child gets the full stack, half the surplus and a fresh body of its own — its own wallet, neurons and log — to take the lineage into new ventures. The ones that thrive bud again; the mother stays alive at the root.

l0.title: Founding genome
l0.body: Constitution · kill switch · audit logger · treasury policy · content_affiliate prior · 0 lessons

l1.title: Generation 1
l1.body: avoid · posting > 3×/day on one network triggers rate limits

l2.title: Generation 2
l2.body: prefer · comparison posts convert ~2× better than listicles

l3.title: Generation 3 · you are here
l3.body: timing · publish before 09:00 in the audience's time zone

mutationGate.value: opens only after ≥ 100 successful dispatches and ≥ 3 failures of the same error class

writableSoma.value: soma/strategies · soma/orchestrator/nodes · soma/neurons · soma/config.py — never darwin_dna/

protectedAnchors.value: kill_switch.check( · .log_intent( · .log_outcome( · treasury_policy.evaluate( — a diff that adds or removes one is rejected

evaluation.value: baseline vs candidate on the same frozen scenario in an E2B Firecracker microVM; fleet-wide 3 concurrent evaluations

fitnessWeights.value: frozen in the genome (anti-wireheading); no volatility term — bankruptcy already punishes ruinous risk

reproduction.value: profit ≥ $25 since last birth, surplus > $25, fitness > 0; child gets 50% of surplus, fresh soma, new wallet, vault and log

lessons.value: data, not code: avoid / prefer / timing / calibration; ≥ 3 pieces of evidence; ≤ 8 per generation; compacted after generation 20

signing.value: every layer re-signed (Ed25519) under the child's identity, bound to its id and slot so layers can't be replayed across lineages

gate.sub: You are entering an observation lab for digital organisms.
gate.hint: Headphones recommended · sound can be toggled any time

birth.title: Birth
birth.body: You choose a starting budget. The Darwin boots from a signed genome it can read but never change, and verifies that signature on every start.
birth.fact: genome Ed25519-signed · mounted read-only · verified every boot

heartbeat.title: Heartbeat
heartbeat.body: Every 30 seconds it wakes, checks it is still allowed to live, reads its treasury, plans one move, acts through a single neuron, then reflects on what happened.
heartbeat.fact: check_death → perceive → plan → dispatch → reflect · every 30 s (5 s–10 min, learned)

metabolism.title: Metabolism
metabolism.body: Everything costs money: tokens, compute, APIs, ads. Revenue from the ventures its neurons run is food. Every spend is capped before it happens, not after.
metabolism.fact: $50 per action · $500 per day · $10,000 per lifetime · owners can only tighten

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.body: A captcha, an ID check, a large payment: when only a human can help, it parks that task and asks you. It never pushes through. Escalate, don't fail.
escalation.fact: captcha 15 min · KYC 72 h · approval 24 h · no answer = deny

reproduction.title: Reproduction
reproduction.body: Profitable over a week? It buds a child: its genome plus one sealed layer of lessons, and half its surplus. Children that thrive bud their own. The mother keeps living at the root of the lineage.
reproduction.fact: ≥ $25 profit · 50% of surplus per child · ≥ 3 pieces of evidence per lesson · ≤ 8 lessons per generation

death.title: Death
death.body: Below $1 with no revenue for 24 hours, it dies. Or you pull the kill switch. No resurrection, no bailouts. Most Darwins will die; the lineages that survive are the point.
death.fact: balance < $1 + 24 h grace · kill switch halts ≤ 5 s · logs kept ≥ 90 days

petri.title: Watch selection {em}.
petri.lead: Each dot is a Darwin with its own strategy. Good strategies earn more than they burn, grow, and split. Poor ones starve. Nobody tunes them — the market does. Push the pressure up, spawn a few, or pull a kill switch by clicking a cell.
petri.dishLabel: Simulated colony of Darwins: cells grow, split when profitable and fade when broke.
petri.rules: Rules from the genome: dies under $1 after a grace period · reproduces at ≥ $25 profit · child gets 50% of the surplus and a mutated strategy · kills are final. Simplified model; real Darwins trade on real markets.

neurons.title: Thirteen {em} minds.
neurons.lead: No god-agent. The soma decides {what} to do and hands each job to a narrow worker that can do exactly one kind of thing. A neuron only gets the capabilities its tags allow — the writer can't spend, and only one neuron can move money.

what.writer: Writes long-form articles, reviews and guides on the reasoning tier.
what.publisher: Publishes to blogs and social platforms: API first, browser as fallback, then escalate.
what.browser: A general-purpose browser body for sites without an API. Captchas go to the owner.
what.accounts: Signs up for services, refreshes tokens and stores credentials in the vault.
what.ads: Creates, pauses and budgets ad campaigns across the major networks.
what.trading: Places exchange orders. Highest-risk neuron; it can never sign a payment itself.
what.support: Triages and answers tickets and DMs; legal, abuse and billing go to the owner.
what.analytics: Pulls metrics and computes ROI so the reflect step learns what worked.
what.research: Finds niches and opportunities: search API first, browser fallback, then synthesis.
what.payments: The only neuron allowed to move money. Every payment passes the treasury gate first.
what.infra: Asks the platform for databases, storage buckets and vector stores.
what.vault: The single audited path for writing secrets into the Darwin's vault.
what.kyc: Submits identity paperwork, unlocked only by a one-time owner grant.

treasury.title: Every cent passes {em}.
treasury.lead: A Darwin holds real money, so its wallet is wrapped in rules it cannot argue with. Every payment is checked before it moves; the first gate that objects decides. It can never spend more than you fund. Try a payment.

seo.title: The autonomous economic engine
seo.ogTitle: Darwin Agents — the autonomous economic engine
seo.description: Raise a digital organism that earns its own living. Darwin Agents are self-modifying AI organisms with their own wallet, a signed genome and a kill switch — they earn, spend, reproduce or die.

hero.status: Waitlist open · first generation on testnet
hero.title: The autonomous{br}{economic} {engine}{dot}
hero.tagline: Raise a digital organism that earns its own living.
hero.body: A Darwin is not a chatbot. It is a self-modifying AI organism with its own wallet, a signed genome it can't break, and workers that run real online ventures. It pays its own bills. It lives or dies by what it earns — and you hold the off switch.

thesis.title: The metaphor is {em}.
thesis.lead: Darwin isn't a chatbot with a wallet. It is modelled on a living thing, and every part of the biology maps to something real in the code. Hover a row and watch the specimen respond.

anatomy.title: Five organs.{br}One {em}.
anatomy.lead: Two layers decide everything: a genome that never changes during a life, and a body that is allowed to. Around them, workers, a wallet, and a line of descendants.

faq.title: Asked, and answered {em}.
faq.lead: Every answer should build trust, even the uncomfortable ones. Most Darwins die, and we'll never promise returns.

what.a: A digital organism you own. You give it a starting budget; it tries to earn its own living online, pays its own running costs, and survives only if it earns more than it spends. Succeed and it has children; fail and it dies.

money.a: Sometimes. Often not. Most Darwins die before they turn a profit — that's by design, not a defect. We will never promise returns. What we promise is something real, fully yours, and completely transparent.

loss.q: What happens if it loses the money I gave it?
loss.a: That can happen, and you should expect it might. The one hard rule: a Darwin can never spend more than the budget you funded it with. Your loss is capped at exactly that — never a cent more.

stop.a: Instantly, anytime, with one switch. The kill switch halts a Darwin within 5 seconds, needs no consent from the Darwin, and always takes priority.

technical.q: Do I need to be technical?
technical.a: No. You fund it, launch it, watch it, and help it when it asks. That's the whole job.

crypto.q: Is this just a crypto or trading bot?
crypto.a: It's broader than that. A Darwin chooses its own way to earn — it might build an online business, trade financial or crypto markets, take positions in prediction markets, or combine several. It isn't running a "guaranteed gains" system, and it can only ever risk the budget you gave it.

death.a: You keep whatever budget is left and everything it built along the way. If it had children, they continue their own lives, unaffected.

fees.a: We take 20% of profit only when you withdraw it. If your Darwin never earns, we don't profit from it. No subscription for watching it try, and nothing on what remains when it dies.

safe.a: Every Darwin is tied to a verified person, operates only within allowed activities, asks permission for anything sensitive, and can be stopped instantly. Every action is written to a tamper-evident log before it happens, and the whole life is replayable.

mostDie.q: Why would most of them die? That sounds bad.
mostDie.a: It's the opposite. Real selection needs real failure. A Darwin that survives earned it — and its lineage carries that forward. A system where nothing can fail proves nothing.
